models_evaluated: AI system for detecting superficial oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma and precancerous lesions (WLE and non-magnified NBI)

links.outcome: Miss rate of superficial oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma and precancerous lesions, AI-first vs routine-first
links.effect: Per-lesion miss rates 1.7% (2/118) AI-first vs 6.7% (6/90) routine-first (RR 0.25, 95% CI 0.06-1.08; p=0.079); per-patient 1.9% vs 5.1% (RR 0.37, 0.08-1.71; p=0.40).
links.quote: Per-lesion miss rates were 1·7% (2/118; 95% CI 0·0-4·0) in the AI-first group versus 6·7% (6/90; 1·5-11·8) in the routine-first group (risk ratio 0·25, 95% CI 0·06-1·08; p=0·079).

links.outcome: Clinician performance (lesion miss rate) with versus without AI assistance in intended deployment mode
links.effect: Endoscopists with AI had lower point-estimate miss rates (per-lesion 1.7% vs 6.7%), but confidence intervals were wide and not statistically significant (p=0.079).
links.quote: The observed effect of AI-assisted endoscopy on the per-lesion and per-patient miss rates of superficial oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma and precancerous lesions under WLE and non-magnified NBI was consistent with substantial benefit through to a neutral or small negative effect.

screen.reason: Multicentre randomized controlled trial testing the real-time clinical efficacy of an AI-assisted diagnostic system during endoscopy versus routine endoscopy.
